# CapacityLens

> Self-hosted resource scheduling and capacity planning for small agencies, by the week. A shared schedule that answers one question: who is free next week?

CapacityLens puts people down the side, days across the top, and the work and time off in between. A day on which someone is booked for more than they can do shows in red, and a separate warning looks 14 days ahead. Utilisation is shown per person for the weeks on screen.

- For: agency owners, studio and operations leads and project managers who decide whether the team can take work on; everyone else on the team sees their own week.
- Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later.
- Cost: free and open source, with no paid tier and no hosted version. The only cost is your own server.
- Requirements: one Linux host with Node 24, an SQLite database file and HTTPS from a proxy on the same machine.
- Status: beta, maintained by one person.
- It does not do: tasks, tickets, deadlines, budgets, timesheets or hour-by-hour scheduling.

Float, Productive, awork, Runn, Teamwork, Resource Guru and eResource Scheduler are good tools, and each covers several jobs, such as budgets, timesheets, project management and reporting. CapacityLens tries to do less: it shows who is busy and who is free, week by week, on a server you run, with no licence fee. If you need budgets, timesheets, hour-level booking or a hosted service, choose one of them.

- [What is CapacityLens?](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/getting-started/what-is-capacitylens.html): the one-page introduction, who it is for and what to know before adopting it
- [Quick start](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/getting-started/quick-start.html): install, create the company and book the first work
- [Install CapacityLens](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/self-hosting/install.html): requirements and installation routes
- [Install without Docker](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/self-hosting/install-without-docker.html): the one-command install and the manual steps
- [Configuration](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/self-hosting/configuration.html): environment settings, including email delivery
- [Upgrades](https://kevinjohn.github.io/capacitylens/self-hosting/upgrades.html): upgrading an installation and what to check afterwards
